To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the spatial topology of the universe can be detected through the circles-in the-sky, and that the knowledge of its value can be used to reduce the degeneracies between the parameters of the dark energy equation of state.

the topological contribution is significant in the analysis of the EOS parameters of a DE model, that it reduces the statistical uncertainties of the EOS parameters, and that it can be considered as an observable quantity, which can be measured through the CMB anisotropy maps.

the topological contribution to the likelihood of the CMB anisotropy data is statistically significant at the 3.2$\sigma$ level and that the topological information is useful for breaking the DE EOS parameter degeneracies, as shown by the reduction of the 68.3\% confidence intervals of the EOS parameters by a factor of $\sim 2$.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the role of the spatial topology of the universe on the determination of the DE EOS parameters, and vice versa.
the possibility of using the topological information to constrain the EOS parameters, which is of particular importance for a better understanding of the nature of the DE.
the possibility of constraining the dark energy equation of state through the cosmic topology.

the topological information is not only useful for the determination of the topology but it is also useful to break the degeneracies between the EOS parameters.
the knowledge of a non-trival spatial topology of the universe would allow a better understanding of the cosmological parameters, and hence, a more precise understanding of the nature of the DE.
, in the case of a Poincar{\'e} dodecagonal topology, the circles-in-the sky are a powerful tool to break degeneracies and to reduce the uncertainties on the EOS parameters.

a topological analysis of the CMB anisotropie maps can be used to break degeneracies in cosmological parameters and to constrain the DE EOS, which are otherwise not possible with the current cosmological datasets.
